settings.title: Settings
account.heading: Account
cardSize.heading: Card size
cardSize.description: Controls the size of the movie/TV show cards on the Movies and TV Shows tabs. One shared setting for both tabs.
sync.movieDescription: Fetches fresh metadata (title, year, poster, plot, genres, cast, rating, runtime) from TMDb for every movie created via TMDb, and updates the locally stored copy. It does not touch your own details (tags, format, audio type, location, owner, serial number). May take a moment depending on the number of movies.
sync.tvDescription: Fetches fresh metadata (name, year, status, poster, plot, genres, cast, rating, season/episode counts) from TMDb for every TV show created via TMDb. It does not touch your own details (tags, format, location, owner, serial number), nor which seasons you own and which episodes you have watched.
sync.tvButton: Update all TV shows from TMDb
sync.abortedNoToken: Sync aborted — check that the backend has a valid TMDB_API_TOKEN.
sync.rateLimited: {synced} of {total} {items} updated, but stopped early because TMDb hit a rate limit. Try again shortly to update the rest.
libBackup.heading: Library export / restore
libBackup.description: Export the entire movie/TV library as a JSON file — to use in another system, or as a way back if the library gets messed up. This is not a full system backup (see below) — only the movie/TV data itself.
libBackup.restoreDescription: Restore replaces the entire current movie/TV library with the contents of a previously exported file — anything not in the file disappears. Choose a file and type GENDAN to confirm.
sysBackup.heading: Full system backup
sysBackup.description: Takes a full low-level backup of the whole system (movies, TV shows, deleted movies/shows, tags, users, counters) — for disaster recovery. Note: your external API keys (TMDb/UPC/Discogs/OMDb/Plex) are not included in the backup and must be re-entered manually under "System settings" below after a restore.
sysBackup.restoreDescription: Restore entire system replaces everything above with the contents of a previous system backup — including user accounts. Choose a file and type GENDAN SYSTEM to confirm.
reset.heading: Reset database
reset.description: Empties the movie/TV library completely (movies, TV shows, deleted movies/shows, tags, serial-number counters, plus Voldby BIO screenings/requests) back to an empty state. Does not touch user accounts or system settings. Irreversible — take a full system backup above first if you want to be able to undo. Confirm with your own password.
reset.done: Reset: {movies} movies, {shows} TV shows and related data removed.
cert.heading: TLS certificate
cert.description: Controls the production HTTPS certificate (Caddy, movie.ll.lan, see DEPLOYMENT.md/BUGS.md #23). Higher risk than the app's other tools — a wrong installation can make the site unreachable over HTTPS. Only meaningful in production.
cert.none: No certificate found (neither installed nor staged).
cert.method1Description: Generates a new key + CSR for external signing (e.g. via your internal CA). The key never leaves the server.
cert.pasteSignedLabel: Paste the signed certificate (PEM) once you have had the CSR signed
cert.method2Description: Alternative to the CSR flow — upload a finished .pfx/.p12 file (cert + key in one file).
cert.pkcs12Passphrase: Passphrase for the PKCS12 file (if any)
cert.installDescription: Replaces the currently running certificate with the one prepared above, and reloads Caddy. Irreversible without a fresh backup of the current certificate — confirm with your own password.
cert.installStarted: Installation started — check that the site still responds over HTTPS in a moment.
serial.heading: Serial number setup
serial.description: Controls which number the next added movie gets, and the step used for numbering future movies. To change a specific movie's serial number, do it in that movie's edit window in the library instead.
serial.adminOnly: Only administrators can change this setup.
deleted.heading: Deleted movies
deleted.description: When a movie is deleted, it is logged here along with its serial number — the number is then free to be reused by a new movie.
deleted.none: No movies have been deleted yet.
sys.heading: System settings
sys.description: External API keys and the Plex integration. Can be set via .env on the server instead — a value set here overrides that, immediately, without a restart. Keys are never shown again once saved, only whether a key is set and from where. The Plex server URL is the exception — it is not a secret, and is therefore shown with its actual value.
sys.plexServerUrlHint: Not a secret — shown as-is, e.g. http://192.168.1.50:32400
sys.primarySourceHint: tried first when scanning, the other three as fallbacks afterwards
plexDiag.heading: Plex connection (troubleshooting)
plexDiag.description: Tests the connection to Plex and shows how many of your movies and TV shows can be matched. Always fetches fresh, bypassing the cache, so a just-corrected URL or token is tried immediately. The badge on the cards is enabled per user under "Show fields" in Movies and TV Shows.
plexDiag.noSections: Plex responded, but no movie or TV libraries were found. Does the token's account have access to the libraries?
plexDiag.noTmdbGuids: Note: none of the items in Plex have a TMDb id. The sections are probably using an older agent — matching therefore falls back to title and year, which is less certain.
plexDiag.unmatchedHint: The first of your titles without a match. If they really are in Plex, it is usually because the title or year differs — compare with what Plex calls them.
audit.heading: Audit log
audit.description: Security/data-relevant actions (role changes, system key updates, OTA updates, backup/restore, cinema scheduling/declines), newest first.
audit.loadError: Could not load the audit log.
deploy.heading: Update from GitHub
deploy.description: Fetches the latest version from GitHub (the main branch), reinstalls dependencies and restarts the server automatically. Only available in production (see DEPLOYMENT.md). Usually takes about a minute — the site is briefly unavailable while the backend restarts.
deploy.timeout: Could not confirm that the update has finished yet — check the server manually (see DEPLOYMENT.md's troubleshooting section) or reload the page shortly.
deploy.upToDate: Already up to date — there was no new version to fetch. Still running build {build}.
users.heading: Users
users.description: Manage who has admin rights, and approve/reject new registrations
users.confirmDelete: Delete the user "{username}" permanently? This cannot be undone.
plexImport.heading: Import from Plex
plexImport.description: Creates everything your Plex server has that the portal does not already have. Metadata comes from TMDb, not from Plex — so imported movies and shows look like everything else in the library. Anything you already have is skipped.
plexImport.tagHint: Applied to everything created, so you can filter the result in the library afterwards. Empty field = no tag.
plexImport.nothingToImport: Nothing new to import — everything in Plex already exists in the portal.
plexImport.previewSummary: {count} can be imported. {present} already exist in the portal.
plexImport.doneSummary: {count} created. {present} already existed in the portal.
plexImport.rateLimited: The import was aborted by a TMDb rate limit. Run it again shortly to fetch the rest — what was already created will not be created twice.
plexImport.confirmHint: Review the list below. If you press Import, they are created as real entries with serial numbers.
plexImport.unmatchedHint: Plex has no TMDb id for these, and searching on title and year did not give exactly one answer. They are not imported — add them manually via scan or TMDb search if you want them.
plexImport.failedHint: These were recognised but could not be created. Try the import again — it is usually a temporary TMDb error.
